decisions.decision: Cancel the November 26 meeting since it falls the day before Thanksgiving.
October 22 will not be a regular committee meeting; the committee will instead do a presentation at a "Smoke Stacks" event at 6pm that date.
No meeting will be held on the 19th (or the following week), to be revisited depending on how far the draft plan has progressed.

The town manager's list of statutory/required town plans (open space & recreation, ADA self-evaluation, hazard mitigation, housing production, comprehensive emergency management) will be shared with the consultant (Ramy) and referenced in the master plan, though responsibility for keeping each current still needs to be assigned.

A member compiled a memo/inventory of town-owned facilities and buildings from GIS records and sent it to Chris Ruth for review, intending it to seed a prioritized capital-projects list for the master plan.

what_happened.line: A member presented a GIS-derived inventory of town-owned facilities to start a prioritized capital-projects list, which the master plan currently lacks.
The committee reviewed the town manager's list of legally required town plans and found several, including hazard mitigation and ADA transition, out of date or unfinished.
No formal votes were taken; the committee is instead reworking its own fall schedule, canceling the meeting before Thanksgiving and swapping one date for a public presentation.
The committee agreed to ask its consultant to verify whether goals already listed in the Open Space and Recreation Plan have actually been completed before carrying them into the master plan.

why_it_matters: A prioritized capital-projects list would feed directly into how the Capital Improvements Committee ranks building and infrastructure projects against its annual funding pool -- the process behind future town-meeting spending votes.
Plans the town is legally required to keep current, such as the ADA transition plan and hazard mitigation plan, can affect compliance obligations and eligibility for related state or federal funding.
The master plan is still in draft feedback stages from multiple boards, so residents will have more opportunities for input before any final document comes to a vote.
